novel_features.name: Tag-Outcome Correlation
novel_features.description: Find which habits actually move your scores: correlate any enhanced tag string with the next-day change in sleep, readiness, or any other metric.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining the enhanced_tags table with daily score tables across months of history — a cross-metric SQL join only possible with the local SQLite store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent needs to surface which user-logged behaviors causally predict next-day recovery metrics, rather than just reporting today's score.

novel_features.name: Personal Baseline Engine
novel_features.description: See today's metric against your personal rolling mean and standard deviation bands — not Oura's population norms, your own history.
novel_features.rationale: Requires computing rolling mean and stddev from local historical records; the API returns only today's absolute value with no personalized context.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent needs to decide whether today's metric is meaningfully low or high for this specific user, not just relative to the general population.

novel_features.name: HRV Trend Analysis
novel_features.description: Track whether overnight HRV is improving or declining: 7-day and 30-day rolling means, coefficient of variation, and a plain-English training-load verdict.
novel_features.rationale: Requires extracting HRV arrays from detailed sleep sessions, computing rolling statistics, and detecting slope direction — all across months of local records.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent managing a training schedule needs a structured HRV signal rather than a single-day reading that is too noisy to act on.

novel_features.name: Training Load vs. Readiness Overlay
novel_features.description: See your accumulated training stress (7-day rolling) alongside readiness scores with a 1-day lag to reveal the recovery debt curve before it peaks.
novel_features.rationale: Requires joining the workouts table and readiness table across a rolling window with lag-offset alignment — a query no single API endpoint can answer.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent needs to recommend rest vs. training based on load-readiness dynamics, not just today's readiness score alone.

novel_features.name: Threshold Alert with Exit Codes
novel_features.description: Exit 1 when a metric has been above or below a threshold for N consecutive days — the scripting primitive that Oura has never exposed.
novel_features.rationale: Requires querying consecutive days from the local store in a single call and returning a machine-readable exit code; no existing tool does this.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this in cron jobs or agent tool-use when you need a binary trigger — act now vs. not yet — based on a multi-day recovery trend.

novel_features.name: Anomaly Detection
novel_features.description: Flag days where any metric fell more than N standard deviations from your personal rolling mean, with z-scores and structured JSON output for agent consumption.
novel_features.rationale: Requires computing per-metric rolling baselines across months of local history and flagging statistical outliers — the API returns only raw values.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this in a weekly health monitoring agent to catch emerging problems automatically before the user notices them in the app.

novel_features.name: Weekly Digest
novel_features.description: One structured call returns the week's metric averages, week-over-week deltas, best and worst recovery days, workout totals, and most-logged tags.
novel_features.rationale: Requires aggregating across five metric tables for a rolling week and computing WoW deltas — a multi-table join that no API endpoint provides.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent produces a weekly health briefing for a coach, journal, or Notion log — it replaces five separate API calls with one structured payload.

novel_features.name: Webhook Listener
novel_features.description: Start a local HTTP server that registers with Oura's webhook API and writes incoming events to the local SQLite store as they arrive.
novel_features.rationale: Requires implementing the Oura webhook registration endpoint and a persistent HTTP handler that writes event payloads to SQLite — no existing tool integrates Oura webhooks with local storage.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this to enable event-driven agents that react to new sleep data as it syncs, rather than polling the API on a fixed schedule.

novel_features.name: Sleep Stage Personal Comparison
novel_features.description: Compare any night's sleep stage durations against your personal 30-day averages, flagging stages that deviate significantly from your own baseline.
novel_features.rationale: Requires computing personal stage averages from the detailed sleep sessions table and joining them against a specific night's records — only possible with the local store.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent needs to identify whether a specific night's sleep architecture was unusual for this user, not just whether the total score was low.

novel_features.name: Pre/Post Event Analysis
novel_features.description: Show all key metrics for N days before and after a named date to measure the health impact of travel, illness, a race, or any life event.
novel_features.rationale: Requires querying the local store for a before-window and after-window relative to an arbitrary date — a two-sided range query that no single API call supports.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this when an agent or user needs to objectively measure whether a specific event (flight, illness, dietary experiment) shifted health metrics.

novel_features.name: Data Gap Audit
novel_features.description: List every day in a date range where expected sync data is missing from the local store — identifies ring non-wear and sync failures before they corrupt analysis.
novel_features.rationale: Detectable only by anti-joining a continuous date series against local store records; the API cannot report data it does not have.
novel_features.why_it_matters: Use this before running any bulk analysis to verify data completeness; exits 1 when gaps are found so agents can abort and alert rather than reporting on incomplete history.

narrative.headline: The only Oura Ring CLI that remembers everything: sync all metrics to local SQLite, correlate habits with scores, detect anomalies, and alert on multi-day recovery deficits no app can surface.
narrative.value_prop: Every existing Oura tool is a thin API wrapper — it answers today's question and forgets the answer. oura-pp-cli syncs all 15+ data types to a local SQLite store, enabling offline queries, cross-metric joins, and time-series analysis that require months of history to be meaningful. The result is a CLI where agents can ask 'does alcohol actually hurt my sleep?' and get a statistically grounded answer, not a raw score.
narrative.auth_narrative:
Oura deprecated Personal Access Tokens in December 2025 — OAuth2 Authorization Code is now the only supported flow, and this CLI does not yet automate that exchange. Register an OAuth application at https://cloud.ouraring.com/oauth/applications, complete the Authorization Code exchange yourself (any OAuth2 client works) to obtain an access_token, then run:

  oura-pp-cli auth set-token <token>

or export OURA_ACCESS_TOKEN=<token> before running any command. Access tokens are valid for 30 days; when one expires, repeat the OAuth2 exchange and re-run 'auth set-token' with the new value. Run 'oura-pp-cli doctor' to verify setup.

quickstart.comment: Verify setup and connectivity before the first sync
Populate the local SQLite store with 30 days of history across all data types
Morning review: sleep, readiness, activity, stress, and SpO2 in one view
See today's readiness annotated against your personal 30-day rolling baseline
Find whether a tagged habit actually correlates with next-day readiness

troubleshoots.fix: Your access token is invalid or missing. Re-run the OAuth2 Authorization Code exchange at https://cloud.ouraring.com/oauth/applications and save the new token with 'oura-pp-cli auth set-token <token>' or 'export OURA_ACCESS_TOKEN=<token>'

troubleshoots.symptom: token expired / 401 Unauthorized after working previously
troubleshoots.fix: Access tokens are valid for 30 days and this CLI does not auto-refresh them; repeat the OAuth2 exchange and re-run 'oura-pp-cli auth set-token <token>' with the new value

troubleshoots.symptom: baseline / correlate / anomalies returns 'not enough history'
troubleshoots.fix: Run 'oura-pp-cli sync --since 90d' to populate more history; these commands need at least 14-30 days of local records
Heartrate returns thousands of samples per day; reduce the window with 'oura-pp-cli sync --resources heartrate --since 7d' or skip it with '--resources daily_sleep,daily_readiness,daily_activity'

narrative.when_to_use: Use oura-pp-cli when an agent needs to reason about health trends across multiple days or weeks rather than fetching today's snapshot. It is the right tool for personalized anomaly detection, habit-outcome correlation, training load management, recovery alerting, and any analysis that requires joining Oura data types together. It is especially useful when an agent is building a health briefing, managing a training schedule, or monitoring for recovery deficits over a multi-day window.
anti_triggers: Writing or editing ring firmware, settings, or hardware configuration (the Oura API is read-only except for tags and webhook subscriptions)
Real-time heart rate monitoring (ring data syncs overnight; there is no streaming HR endpoint for live use)
Accessing another user's health data (OAuth scopes are per-user; this CLI is single-account by design)
Complex statistical modeling beyond trend lines and correlations (use a data science environment like pandas or R after exporting via 'oura-pp-cli query')

recipes.title: Morning agent briefing
recipes.explanation: Structured morning snapshot for an AI agent to summarize in a daily briefing; --select keeps the payload compact.

recipes.title: Weekly health digest for coach or journal
recipes.explanation: One call returns the week's averages, WoW deltas, best/worst recovery days, and top tags — ready to paste into Notion or send to a health coach.

recipes.title: Habit correlation analysis
recipes.explanation: Find statistically grounded evidence for whether a tracked habit improves sleep; --select exposes only the fields an agent needs to make a recommendation.

recipes.title: Recovery alerting in cron or CI
recipes.explanation: Exits 0 (condition not met) or 1 (readiness below 70 for 3+ consecutive days); wire into a shell script or agent tool-use to trigger a rest-day recommendation.

recipes.title: Training load check before a workout
recipes.explanation: Surface the accumulated training stress vs. recovery curve so an agent can recommend rest, reduced effort, or full training based on the ratio.

am I recovered enough to train
